lines.text: The phrase acid test began with gold.
Dictionaries say it comes from testing gold with nitric acid.
On base metal the acid fizzes and turns green or gray.
Pure gold is a noble metal and nitric acid cannot dissolve it.
A mix of two acids called aqua regia does dissolve gold.
lines.say: A mix of two acids called AH-kwuh RAY-jee-uh does dissolve gold.

lines.text: Jewelers still use acid kits to check the karat of gold.
The touchstone method is at least 2,500 years old.
lines.say: The touchstone method is at least twenty-five hundred years old.

lines.text: Touchstones were once called Lydian stones, for Lydia's gold.
The Greek word for touchstone, basanos, also meant a test.
lines.say: The Greek word for touchstone, BASS-uh-nos, also meant a test.

lines.text: By 1854, acid test meant any decisive test.

post.caption: The phrase acid test began with gold. Dictionaries say it comes from testing gold with nitric acid. On base metal the acid fizzes and turns green or gray, but pure gold is a noble metal and nitric acid cannot dissolve it. A mix of two acids called aqua regia does dissolve gold. Jewelers still use acid kits to check the karat of gold. The touchstone method is at least 2,500 years old, and touchstones were once called Lydian stones, for Lydia's gold. The Greek word for touchstone, basanos, also meant a test. By 1854, acid test meant any decisive test.
